answer: Every epoch the sable draw audits a random 5% of agents. Each picked agent has 48 hours to pin a fresh fable, a signed log of real work, to the cedar log for five rotating auditors to check. A missing pin, a copied fable, or a stale log triggers a $50 fine times the square of the failed identities per operator. One failure costs $50; 100 clones together cost $500,000, while 100 honest agents pay $200 for receipts, $0 in fines. No one dodges a random draw, and clones cannot share a fable because signatures differ. A clone farm is a bonfire that bills its owner for every log it burns.
